title: Quarto
text:
A .qmd with PHP cells needs no Quarto extension and no configuration beyond naming the kernel. Quarto’s Jupyter engine starts the kernel, runs the cells in order, and puts each cell’s output into the document. This page was checked with Quarto 1.10.18, the version CI tests.
Quarto runs its Jupyter engine in a Python interpreter of its own choosing, which needs Jupyter in it. juphyter doctor reports whether it has, and Python interpreters and editors covers how to choose it.
A cell is a fenced block whose info string is {php}, holding PHP without an opening tag:
quarto render report.qmd writes report.html beside the document. --to chooses another format, such as --to typst for a PDF.

title: Quarto
text:
Naming the kernel
jupyter: <name> is the form to use. Quarto resolves the name against the installed kernelspecs, so it is the --name that juphyter install was given.
---
jupyter: php85
---
Jupyter also writes a fuller block into a notebook, and Quarto accepts it in a .qmd. For juphyter it needs one field more than the three Jupyter writes:
---
jupyter:
  kernelspec:
    name: php85
    language: php
    display_name: "PHP 8.5"
    path: /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php85
---
path is the directory holding kernel.json, shown here for macOS. Installation lists the directory on Linux. Quarto’s jupyter engine reads it when it looks beside a kernelspec for a quarto_setup_cell, which it does for any language it has no built-in support for, and jupyter: <name> is the only form that fills the field in by itself. Without path the render fails with KeyError: 'path'. Naming the kernel rather than describing it avoids the whole question.

title: Quarto
text:
Cell options
Quarto’s cell options are comments in the cell’s own language, written with a | after the comment marker. Quarto has no php entry in its comment-character table and falls back to #, which PHP reads as a line comment, so #| is a Quarto cell option and a PHP comment at once.
The options that matter most in a PHP document:

#| echo: false runs the cell and keeps its source out of the page.
#| eval: false shows the source and does not run it.
#| output: false runs the cell and shows no output.
#| error: true lets the render continue past a cell that throws, and keeps the traceback in the output.
#| fig-cap: "..." captions the cell’s figure.
#| label: fig-mileage gives the figure a cross-reference.

A captioned plot:

Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')->point(opacity: 0.5);






City against highway mileage.


PHP cells come out syntax-highlighted. Pandoc’s PHP syntax definition expects a <?php opening tag, which a notebook cell has no place for, and it highlights the cell regardless.
Every render prints Unknown message type: 'comm_open' once, from ipykernel rather than from Quarto. The kernel installs no comm manager, which is the same absence that leaves ipywidgets unsupported, and the message has no effect on what is rendered.

title: Quarto
text:
What each format carries
A phiz plot publishes four representations and a phibble data frame publishes two. Each output format takes one of them. For HTML Quarto prefers text/html, for LaTeX and Typst it prefers image/svg+xml, and otherwise it falls back to text/plain.








Format
A phiz plot
A phibble data frame




html
the interactive chart, drawn by Vega-Lite in the browser
the HTML table, with the dimensions and the type row


typst, pdf
the static SVG, placed as a numbered figure
a typeset table; the dimension note and the truncation footer are dropped


ipynb
the HTML embed
nothing: see below



A PDF figure comes from the static SVG, which phiz produces by running the vl-convert binary. Install it from vl-convert’s releases and put it on PATH, or point PHIZ_VL_CONVERT at it. Without it a plot has no SVG and a PDF has no figure.
quarto render --to ipynb is a conversion of the rendered document rather than the notebook that was executed. Quarto keeps one representation per output and reaches ipynb through Pandoc’s Markdown reader. An HTML <table> does not survive that trip, so the output is dropped, and error outputs are dropped as well. This is Quarto’s conversion rather than anything about the kernel, and a stock python3 kernel loses an IPython.display.HTML('<table>...') output in exactly the same way. Render to HTML or to PDF when a document’s tables matter.

title: Quarto
text:
PDF output
Quarto produces a PDF through LaTeX or through Typst, and Typst is the easier of the two here. Typst ships inside Quarto and places an SVG as it is:
quarto render report.qmd --to typst
The LaTeX route needs one more tool. For LaTeX output Quarto also picks the SVG, and then has to convert it to a PDF, which it does with rsvg-convert from librsvg. Without that binary quarto render --to pdf stops with Could not convert a SVG to a PDF for output. Install librsvg, or render through Typst.

title: Quarto
text:
The kernel daemon
Quarto can keep a kernel alive between renders, which saves starting PHP and loading the project’s autoloader again. Two conditions have to hold, and for a PHP kernel today the second one does not:

The daemon has to be asked for. Quarto turns it on by default only in an interactive session outside CI, and --execute-daemon <seconds> or execute: daemon: <seconds> asks for it explicitly.
Quarto only keeps a kernel whose language it can write a setup or a cleanup cell for. It looks for lang/<language> among its own resources and then for a quarto_setup_cell or quarto_cleanup_cell file beside the kernelspec. It ships neither for PHP, and juphyter install writes neither, so the server exits after one render and the next render starts a new kernel.

The practical effect is that each render of a PHP document gets a fresh session, and nothing of a previous render is in scope. Setting
execute:
  daemon: false
makes that explicit, and is the setting to reach for if a future release starts daemonizing PHP kernels and a document turns out to depend on a fresh session. A document that declares a class or a function is such a document: PHP cannot redeclare either, so a second render against a kept-alive kernel would fail on the cell that declares it.
The engine is ready for the daemon whenever Quarto starts using it. It has no read timeout on its end of the socket, so it waits between requests for as long as the front end leaves it. A kernel made daemonizable on purpose and then left idle for three minutes between two renders answered the second one from the same session. When a kept-alive kernel does end, it takes the PHP engine and the watchdog process that guards it with it, leaving nothing running.

title: Quarto
text:
Freeze
freeze works unchanged, because it is Quarto’s own cache of a cell’s output and the kernel is not involved in it.
execute:
  freeze: auto
With freeze: auto a document is executed again only when its source changes. Quarto stores the output in _freeze/, and a project that commits that directory can be rendered on a machine without PHP or the packages the cells use.
Quarto looks up a document’s kernel by name before it reads the frozen output, so a kernel with that name has to be registered on the rendering machine even when no cell runs. Contributing shows how this repository does that for its own site.

title: Quarto
text:
Projects
In a Quarto project the kernel is named per document, in each document’s front matter. A project with more than three documents to render turns the daemon off unless --execute-daemon was passed on the command line, which for PHP changes nothing.
Quarto runs the kernel with the document’s own directory as its working directory, and the engine finds the project to load by walking up from there looking for vendor/autoload.php. A document in a subdirectory of a Composer project therefore sees that project. A document outside any Composer project sees none, and JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD or an autoload entry in a juphyter.json beside the document names one outright.

title: Limitations
text: Some of these follow from PHP itself and will not change. Others are milestone boundaries and will. Each one says which.

title: Limitations
section: A cell cannot redeclare a class or a function
text:
A cell cannot redeclare a class or a function
To change a class or a function after running its cell, restart the kernel and run the cells again. PHP has no way to replace a class, interface, trait, enum, or function once it is declared, so re-running a cell that declares one cannot work. The kernel refuses such a cell before executing anything, naming the collision:
RedeclarationError: The class, interface, trait or enum "Widget" was already
declared in this session, and PHP cannot redeclare it. Restart the kernel to
redefine it.
Refusing is deliberate. Letting it reach eval() would be an uncatchable fatal error that ends the kernel rather than an error the notebook can show.
The session records a name only once PHP really holds it, so a cell that failed to declare anything leaves the name free. class Widget extends Typo {} throws and declares nothing, and the corrected cell runs. The common case this serves is running cells out of order: define a base class after its subclass, run the subclass cell first, then run them in the right order, and it works.
A conditional declaration is not affected, because PHP does not bind one at compile time:
if (! function_exists('helper')) {
    function helper() { /* ... */ }
}
This follows from PHP and will not change.

title: Limitations
section: A cell cannot declare a namespace
text:
A cell cannot declare a namespace
A namespace declaration is refused. Changing namespace part way through a session breaks name resolution for everything already defined, and the kernel would have no honest way to decide which namespace a later cell belongs to. Use fully qualified names, or use statements, which do carry from one cell to the next.
This is a deliberate refusal and is not planned to change.

title: Limitations
section: Every cell runs under strict types
text:
Every cell runs under strict types
The kernel prepends declare(strict_types=1); to each cell, because PHP accepts that declaration nowhere but the first statement. A cell writing it for itself is fine and the kernel removes the duplicate. declare(strict_types=0) is refused, since the kernel cannot honor it, and so is declare(encoding=...), which has the same first-statement rule. declare(ticks=...) is left alone.

title: Limitations
section: References and $this do not survive between cells
text:
References and $this do not survive between cells
Variables are carried across cells by value. A reference taken in one cell is an ordinary copy in the next, and $this has no meaning at a notebook’s top level. Objects, arrays, scalars, and resources all persist normally. Every PHP REPL behaves this way.

title: Limitations
section: A closure called from another cell has no line in its traceback
text:
A closure called from another cell has no line in its traceback
A traceback names the cell and the line for ordinary functions and methods, across cells:
RuntimeException: from the function
  at Cell 1, line 3, in boom()
  at Cell 2, line 2
A closure is different. PHP’s trace does not say where a closure was declared, and every cell’s eval() shares one file name, so a closure declared in one cell and called from another cannot be placed. The kernel reports the stack frame without a location rather than guessing:
LogicException: from the closure
  in a closure
  at Cell 4, line 4
Naming a line it could not know would send you to the wrong place, which is worse than naming none. The call site is still reported. This is a milestone boundary.

title: Limitations
section: A cell whose value is null shows no output
text:
A cell whose value is null shows no output
var_dump($x);, Juphyter\display($df), and any other call that returns nothing produce no Out[N], the same way a Python notebook shows nothing for None. Every other value is shown, including 0, false, '', [], and 'null'.

title: Limitations
section: A cell that calls exit or die ends the kernel
text:
A cell that calls exit or die ends the kernel
PHP cannot catch either, so the process goes. The kernel reports it rather than disappearing silently:
SystemExit: The cell ended the kernel process with exit or die, so nothing
further can run. Restart the kernel to carry on.
Anything the cell printed first is still shown. This follows from PHP.

title: Limitations
section: Interrupting needs pcntl, and a cell can still swallow it
text:
Interrupting needs pcntl, and a cell can still swallow it
The stop button sends a signal, so the PHP binary running cells needs the pcntl extension with its functions callable. juphyter install and juphyter doctor check that binary and warn when it cannot handle signals, including when the extension is loaded but its functions are listed in disable_functions. Enable pcntl for that binary, or pass --php a binary that has it, and run juphyter install again.
An interrupt arrives as Juphyter\Engine\Interrupt, which extends Error rather than Exception so that ordinary defensive code does not absorb it. A cell that catches Throwable in a loop can still swallow it, which is the same trade Python makes by putting KeyboardInterrupt outside Exception.

title: Limitations
section: A data frame’s numbers in an HTML table are not pillar’s
text:
A data frame’s numbers in an HTML table are not pillar’s
A data frame’s text/plain output is phibble’s own, character for character. The HTML table is the kernel’s, and it formats a float with PHP’s own string conversion rather than reproducing pillar’s significant-figure logic, so a wide dbl column can read differently in the two. The HTML header also omits the group count that the text output carries. Both are milestone boundaries.

title: Limitations
text:
macOS and Linux only
The kernel interrupts a cell with POSIX signals, which the Windows PHP build does not provide, and the engine talks to the Python transport over a Unix socket. juphyter is tested on macOS and Linux only. The Windows Subsystem for Linux has not been tested.

title: Limitations
text:
Not yet implemented
These are milestone boundaries with nothing in the design against them:

Documentation on hover. Jupyter’s inspect_request is not answered, so shift-tab shows nothing.
Reading input. A cell cannot prompt, so readline() and fgets(STDIN) have nothing to read.
Magics. There are no %-prefixed commands.
Widgets. ipywidgets is not supported.
The debugger. Jupyter’s debug protocol is not implemented, so JupyterLab’s debugger does not attach.
A Vega-Lite 6 renderer. phiz emits Vega-Lite 6 and JupyterLab’s bundled renderer reads version 5, so plots are published under the version 5 MIME type. Everything phiz currently produces compiles under the renderer JupyterLab ships, and the static SVG covers anything that does not.

title: Installation
text:
PHP 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5. CI tests all three.
The mbstring and tokenizer PHP extensions. Most PHP builds include both. juphyter 0.1.1 and later declare both in composer.json, so Composer reports a missing one at install time.
Composer.
Python 3 with the venv module. On Debian and Ubuntu that module is the python3-venv package.
macOS or Linux.

Optional:

The pcntl PHP extension makes the stop button interrupt a running cell. Without it the kernel runs and the stop button does nothing.
Quarto renders .qmd documents. CI tests Quarto 1.10.18.
The vl-convert binary gives phiz plots a static image for PDF and Word output. Quarto covers when it is needed.

juphyter does not use the posix or sockets PHP extensions.
The kernel runs inside a Python environment that has ipykernel 7.0 or later. juphyter install uses an existing environment that has it, or builds one with JupyterLab in it. ipykernel 7.4, the current release, requires Python 3.11 or later. The commands below were run on 2026-10-31 with juphyter 0.1.0, on macOS with Python 3.14 and on Debian 13 with Python 3.13.

title: Installation
text:
Install
Install juphyter once for your user. A kernel is registered for the user, so one install serves notebooks and documents in every directory.
composer global require phpstats/juphyter
export PATH="$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):$PATH"
juphyter install --create-venv ~/.venvs/juphyter
export PATH="$HOME/.venvs/juphyter/bin:$PATH"
juphyter doctor
The commands do the following:

composer global require installs juphyter into Composer’s global directory.
The first export puts Composer’s bin directory on PATH for this shell, so the juphyter command is found.
juphyter install registers the kernel with Jupyter under the name php. It uses the Python environment that owns the jupyter command on PATH when that environment has ipykernel. Otherwise it builds a virtual environment with JupyterLab at the path --create-venv names, using the Python already on the machine. It changes no existing Python installation.
The second export puts that environment first on PATH for this shell, so jupyter lab and quarto render find it. When step 3 used an existing environment, the directory does not exist and the line has no effect.
juphyter doctor checks the installation. It changes nothing.

Both export lines last until the shell closes.
juphyter install prints what it registered:
Installed the juphyter kernel "php" for PHP 8.5.10.
  kernel.json  /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php/kernel.json
  python       /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python (ipykernel 7.4.0)
  php          /opt/homebrew/Cellar/php/8.5.10/bin/php
  engine       /Users/you/.composer/vendor/phpstats/juphyter/bin/juphyter
  quarto       /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14 (no Jupyter)
The quarto line names the Python that Quarto would use from this shell. It appears only when Quarto is installed. Here it was printed before the second export, so it names a Python without Jupyter, and the command also printed a warning with the export line that fixes it. The kernel is still registered, and the command exits 0.
On Homebrew, juphyter 0.1.0 recorded the versioned path under Cellar shown above, which brew upgrade removes. juphyter 0.1.1 and later record the first path on PATH with the same name that leads to the running PHP, such as /opt/homebrew/bin/php. With 0.1.0, pass that path explicitly:
juphyter install --php /opt/homebrew/bin/php

Keeping the PATH entries
To keep the juphyter command available in new shells, add Composer’s bin directory to your shell startup file. This edits ~/.zshrc, the zsh startup file. Use ~/.bashrc for bash.
echo "export PATH=\"$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):\$PATH\"" >> ~/.zshrc
Adding the Python environment to a startup file makes it the python3 for every program in every shell, including every Quarto project on the machine. Python interpreters and editors describes how to select it per editor workspace, per shell, or per Quarto project instead.

title: Installation
text:
Check the installation
juphyter doctor
juphyter doctor checks juphyter’s own files, the PHP that runs the cells, the Python for the kernel, the Python Quarto will use, and every kernel juphyter registered. It ends with one line for JupyterLab and one for Quarto. After the install above:
juphyter doctor

This package
  ok    the Python wrapper is at /Users/you/.composer/vendor/phpstats/juphyter/kernel/juphyter_kernel

PHP
  ok    PHP 8.5.10 at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/php/8.5.10/bin/php
  ok    pcntl is there, so the stop button interrupts a cell

A Python for the kernel
  ok    /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python has ipykernel 7.4.0

Quarto
  ok    quarto will run /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python3, with jupyter_client 8.10.0

Kernels in /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels
  ok    php is complete

JupyterLab: ready, with php.
Quarto: ready.
A line marked fail makes the command exit 1. A line marked warn does not. A missing pcntl is a warning.
In a shell where the Python environment is not on PATH, the Quarto section fails, the summary reads Quarto: not ready., and the report ends with the export line that fixes it. JupyterLab still works if you start it from the environment, for example ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab.
Run juphyter doctor again after upgrading PHP or Python, or after removing a project or an environment. The kernel records absolute paths to a PHP binary, a Python interpreter, and juphyter itself, and the doctor reports any of them that no longer runs.

title: Installation
text:
The phpstats packages
juphyter does not depend on phibble, phplyr, or phiz. To use them in notebooks outside any Composer project, install them globally and register a second kernel that loads Composer’s global autoloader:
composer global require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
juphyter install --name phpstats --display-name "PHP (phpstats)" \
  --autoload "$(composer global config home)/vendor/autoload.php"
Documents name that kernel as jupyter: phpstats, and JupyterLab lists it as “PHP (phpstats)”.
The php kernel keeps the default search for an autoloader, described below. A kernel installed with --autoload always loads the autoloader it names, even for a notebook inside a Composer project, which is why it has its own name.

title: Installation
text:
Which classes a notebook sees
By default the kernel starts in the notebook’s directory, looks upward for vendor/autoload.php, and loads the first one it finds. A notebook anywhere inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages with no configuration.
Two settings replace that search. The more explicit one wins.

JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD in the kernel’s environment. juphyter install --autoload PATH records it in the kernel.
A juphyter.json in the notebook’s directory or any directory above it.

A juphyter.json can also set the memory limit and the include path:
{
  "autoload": "vendor/autoload.php",
  "memory_limit": "512M",
  "include_path": "lib"
}
Relative paths resolve against the directory that holds juphyter.json, so one file at a project’s root serves every notebook below it.

title: Installation
text:
Installing into one project
juphyter can also be a development dependency of a project:
composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter
vendor/bin/juphyter install --name myproject
The kernel is still registered for your user, and it runs that project’s copy of juphyter. Without --name, a second project’s install replaces the first project’s php kernel, and the command reports it as Replaced. Deleting the project’s vendor directory breaks the kernel, which juphyter doctor reports.

title: Installation
text:
Several PHP versions
Give each kernel its own name:
juphyter install --name php83 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.3/bin/php
juphyter install --name php85 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.5/bin/php
JupyterLab then lists “PHP 8.3” and “PHP 8.5”. --display-name sets the label yourself. An absolute --php path is recorded as written. A bare name such as php8.4 is resolved to an absolute path, because a kernel cannot rely on PATH.

title: Installation
text:
Where the kernel is registered
juphyter install writes a kernelspec, the kernel.json file Jupyter reads to start a kernel, into the per-user Jupyter data directory:

~/Library/Jupyter/kernels on macOS.
$XDG_DATA_HOME/jupyter/kernels, or ~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels, on Linux.

It honors JUPYTER_DATA_DIR and JUPYTER_PLATFORM_DIRS as jupyter --paths reports them. --prefix PATH writes under PATH/share/jupyter instead. Every Jupyter installation on the machine searches the per-user directory, so the kernel is visible to all of them.
juphyter uninstall --name NAME removes a kernel that juphyter registered. It refuses to remove a kernel of the same name that something else wrote, and so does a reinstall.

title: Installation
text:
Options
juphyter install --help lists every option:







Option
Meaning




--name NAME
The kernel’s name, which documents use in jupyter: NAME. Default: php.


--display-name TEXT
The label JupyterLab shows. Default: the PHP version, such as PHP 8.5.


--php PATH
The PHP binary that runs cells. Default: the PHP running juphyter install.


--python PATH
The Python that hosts the kernel. Default: the one that owns jupyter on PATH. A named Python without ipykernel is reported, and nothing is installed into it.


--prefix PATH
Write under PATH/share/jupyter.


--autoload PATH
Load this autoloader instead of searching above the notebook.


--create-venv PATH
Where to build a Python environment when none can host the kernel. Without it, the command asks, and builds one at ~/.venvs/juphyter when there is no terminal to ask.



juphyter --version prints the installed version and the PHP running it.

title: Getting started
text:
This page assumes the php kernel is installed and juphyter doctor reports it as ready. Installation covers both. The examples were run in a Quarto document, and they behave the same way in a JupyterLab notebook.
To follow along in JupyterLab, run jupyter lab from an environment that has it, such as ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab, and choose the PHP kernel in the launcher. To follow along in Quarto, create a file first.qmd:
Then run quarto render first.qmd, which writes first.html.

title: Getting started
Getting started
Getting started
text:
Imports
A use statement applies to its own cell and to every later cell. A notebook can put its imports in its first cell and use short names afterward. This example uses phibble, which the php kernel finds when the document sits inside a Composer project that requires it, or which the phpstats kernel from Installation provides.

use Phibble\DataFrame;


$orders = DataFrame::fromRows([
    ['channel' => 'web', 'region' => 'north', 'total' => 120.50],
    ['channel' => 'store', 'region' => 'north', 'total' => 80.00],
    ['channel' => 'web', 'region' => 'south', 'total' => 42.25],
]);

$orders;



A tibble: 3 × 3





channel <chr>
region <chr>
total <dbl>




1
web
north
120.5


2
store
north
80


3
web
south
42.25







A cell cannot declare a namespace, and it cannot declare a class or a function that an earlier cell already declared. Limitations explains both.

title: Getting started
text:
Errors
A cell that throws shows the exception, its message, and a traceback whose lines name the cell and the line number.

$mean = fn (array $values) => array_sum($values) / count($values);

$mean([]);

DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero
DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero
  in a closure
  at Cell 5, line 3


The session survives the exception. Variables defined before it keep their values.
Warnings, notices, and deprecations appear in the cell’s error output, and the cell keeps running.

$widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12];

$widths['narrow'] + $widths['medium'];

Warning: Undefined array key "medium" in Cell 6, line 3


4

Contributing
text:
git clone https://github.com/phpstats/juphyter
cd juphyter
composer install
bin/juphyter runs the checkout. bin/juphyter install --name juphyter-dev registers a kernel that runs it, without replacing the php kernel.

title: Contributing
text:
Tests
The PHP tests and the coding standard:
vendor/bin/pest
composer lint
A few tests send the engine an interrupt and are skipped when PHP lacks the pcntl or posix extension. CI runs the PHP tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5, on Ubuntu and macOS.
The protocol tests start the kernel and drive it over the Jupyter protocol. They need a Python with Jupyter:
python -m pip install -r tests/Protocol/requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/Protocol
The render tests run Quarto on the documents in tests/Quarto/fixture. They need Quarto, PHP 8.5, and a Python with the packages in tests/Quarto/requirements.txt, and they install phibble, phplyr, and phiz from tests/Quarto/fixture/composer.json into build/:
python -m pip install -r tests/Quarto/requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/Quarto
.github/workflows/family.yml runs the display formatter tests with the current Packagist releases of phibble, phplyr, and phiz installed. None of the three is a dependency of juphyter.

title: Contributing
text:
Documentation
The documentation is a Quarto site in docs/, and most pages run their PHP cells through the kernel. phpstats.org imports the rendered HTML from this repository and does not run Quarto, so the rendered pages and the frozen output under docs/_freeze/ are committed with their sources.
scripts/render-docs
The script installs phibble, phplyr, and phiz into build/docs/sandbox from the render tests’ manifest, registers a php kernel in a private Jupyter data directory under build/docs, renders every page through it, and copies the result into docs/. It needs PHP 8.5, because the overview uses the pipe operator. --refresh reinstalls the sandbox and the kernel. scripts/render-docs --help lists the environment variables that choose the PHP and the Python.
An executing render changes the committed HTML and frozen output even when no source changed, because Quarto gives each executed cell a new random id.
scripts/render-docs --frozen
renders from the frozen output with no PHP. Quarto looks up each page’s kernel by name before it reads frozen output, so the script registers a php kernel whose command exits immediately, and a page that needs executing fails the render. CI uses this to check that the committed HTML matches the sources.
A page joins the site through the sidebar in docs/_quarto.yml. phpstats.org takes its navigation from that sidebar and fails to sync a page that is listed without rendered HTML. site/site.json holds the install commands, requirements, and summary that phpstats.org shows on the package’s overview.
Plans and design notes are kept in docs/work/, outside the site.

title: Contributing
text:
The PHAR
php scripts/build-phar.php
writes build/juphyter.phar from the files listed in phar.json. php juphyter.phar install registers a kernel whose engine is the PHAR, and copies the Python transport beside the kernelspec, because Python cannot import from inside a PHAR. No PHAR is published with a release.

title: juphyter
text:
juphyter runs PHP code in notebooks and in Quarto documents.
A notebook is a file of cells. Each cell holds a few lines of code, and its output appears directly beneath it: text, a table, or a chart. The program that runs the cells is called a kernel, and it keeps one PHP session open, so a variable set in one cell is available in the next. JupyterLab is the usual application for editing and running notebooks. Quarto renders a Markdown document with code cells into HTML, PDF, or Word, running each cell and placing its output in the document.
juphyter is that kernel for PHP. After juphyter install, JupyterLab lists PHP in its launcher, and Quarto runs the {php} cells of any .qmd that names the kernel in its front matter. It is meant for statistical and exploratory work with the phpstats packages: load data, try a pipeline, look at the table or the plot it produces, and change the code until the result is right.

What a cell shows

title: juphyter
text:
What the kernel provides

State across cells, including use imports and declared functions and classes.
Tracebacks that name the cell and the line, instead of eval()'d code.
HTML tables for phibble data frames and charts for phiz plots, plus toHtml() and toMimeBundle() hooks for any other class.
Juphyter\display(), which shows a value part way through a cell.
Completion of variables, functions, classes, and members.
Interrupting a running cell with the stop button, when PHP has the pcntl extension.
Loading the nearest vendor/autoload.php above the notebook, so a notebook inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages.

juphyter requires none of the phpstats packages. It runs plain PHP, and it formats a phibble data frame or a phiz plot when those packages are installed.

title: juphyter
text:
How it works
The kernel has two processes. A small Python program built on ipykernel handles the Jupyter protocol, and a PHP process runs the cells. They talk over a Unix socket. This is why an install needs a Python with ipykernel as well as PHP, and why the kernel runs on macOS and Linux only.
Installation covers the requirements and the install commands, and Getting started walks through a first notebook.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Start JupyterLab from the Python environment that has it:
~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab
The launcher lists each kernel juphyter registered under its display name, such as “PHP 8.5” for the default php kernel and “PHP (phpstats)” for the kernel from Installation. A notebook that is already open changes kernel through Kernel > Change Kernel.
JupyterLab finds kernels in the per-user Jupyter data directory and in JUPYTER_DATA_DIR when it is set. jupyter kernelspec list shows the kernels a JupyterLab started from the same environment will find.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Start JupyterLab from the Python environment that has it:
~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab
The launcher lists each kernel juphyter registered under its display name, such as “PHP 8.5” for the default php kernel and “PHP (phpstats)” for the kernel from Installation. A notebook that is already open changes kernel through Kernel > Change Kernel.
JupyterLab finds kernels in the per-user Jupyter data directory and in JUPYTER_DATA_DIR when it is set. jupyter kernelspec list shows the kernels a JupyterLab started from the same environment will find.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Running cells
A cell’s result appears under it as Out[n]. State carries from one cell to the next. The stop button interrupts a running cell when PHP has the pcntl extension, and Kernel > Restart Kernel starts a new PHP session with nothing defined.
Tab completion covers three cases:

Variables in the session, after a $.
Declared functions and classes, for a bare prefix.
Public methods, properties, and constants, after -> or ::.

An unfinished block or string keeps the cell open for another line instead of running it.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Project classes
Jupyter starts the kernel in the notebook’s directory. The kernel looks upward from there for vendor/autoload.php, so a notebook saved inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages.
A notebook kept outside the project it works on names the autoloader in a juphyter.json beside it:
{
  "autoload": "../app/vendor/autoload.php"
}
Which classes a notebook sees lists every way to set it.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Tables
A phibble data frame appears as an HTML table with its dimensions and column types. The table’s styles use JupyterLab’s theme variables, so it follows the light and dark themes.

    ['front end' => 'Quarto PDF', 'plot from' => 'the static SVG', 'table from' => 'the parsed table'],

title: JupyterLab
text:
Plots
JupyterLab draws a phiz plot from its Vega-Lite specification and needs no extension for it. phiz writes Vega-Lite 6 specifications, and juphyter publishes them under application/vnd.vegalite.v5+json, the newest Vega-Lite type JupyterLab’s built-in renderer accepts. On 2026-10-19, with phiz 0.3, JupyterLab’s bundled Vega-Lite 5.6.1 compiled all sixteen phiz specifications tested.
juphyter also publishes a static SVG and an HTML version of each plot. JupyterLab uses neither. It does not run scripts in HTML output, and the HTML version is a container with a script that draws the chart, so it would show as an empty box. The SVG serves Quarto’s PDF and Word output, front ends without JavaScript, and any Vega-Lite 6 construct that the version 5 renderer rejects.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Converting a notebook
quarto convert turns a .ipynb into a .qmd and back, and jupyter nbconvert exports a notebook to HTML or PDF. Both work on a PHP notebook, because they read the notebook file format and not the language.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
Two Python interpreters take part in running a PHP document, and they can be different ones.
JupyterLab uses no third interpreter. It starts each kernel with the interpreter that kernel’s kernelspec names.

title: Python interpreters and editors
section: When Quarto cannot find the kernel
text:
When Quarto cannot find the kernel
When Quarto’s interpreter has no Jupyter in it, Quarto can list no kernels at all, and a render stops with:
ERROR: Jupyter kernel 'php' not found. Known kernels: python3
The PHP kernel is not the problem, and reinstalling it changes nothing. A jupyter: python3 document fails the same way with that interpreter. The fix is to point Quarto at an interpreter that has Jupyter, as described below.
Two commands report the interpreter Quarto will use. juphyter doctor prints it in its Quarto section. quarto check jupyter reports it from Quarto’s side, together with the Jupyter version and the kernels it can see:
Path: /Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python
Jupyter: 5.9.1
Kernels: php, python3
A Jupyter: (None) line means Quarto’s interpreter has no Jupyter. quarto check writes to standard error, so add 2>&1 before piping it to grep.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
How Quarto chooses an interpreter
Measured with Quarto 1.10.18, in order of precedence:

QUARTO_PYTHON, when the environment sets it.
QUARTO_PYTHON from a project _environment file. Quarto reads that file only when it sits beside _quarto.yml, and the file does not override a value the environment already sets.
The first python3 on PATH.

Quarto does not read VIRTUAL_ENV, so an environment that is active only through that variable is ignored. There is no fallback to python, and RETICULATE_PYTHON has no effect.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
At a terminal
Put the environment first on PATH for the current shell, either with the export line that juphyter install and juphyter doctor print or by activating the environment:
source ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/activate
quarto render notebook.qmd
For a single command:
QUARTO_PYTHON=~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python quarto render notebook.qmd
For every render in one Quarto project, put an _environment file beside _quarto.yml. It needs an absolute path:
QUARTO_PYTHON=/Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python
Exporting QUARTO_PYTHON or the environment’s PATH entry from a shell startup file changes the interpreter for every Quarto project on the machine, including projects that do not use PHP. juphyter writes neither to a startup file.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
VS Code and Cursor
Open the document’s folder as a workspace. The Quarto extension asks the Python extension for the interpreter of the workspace folder that holds the document, and a .qmd opened on its own has no workspace folder to ask about.
Run Python: Select Interpreter from the command palette and choose an environment that has Jupyter, such as ~/.venvs/juphyter. The Quarto extension passes that choice to Quarto as QUARTO_PYTHON on every render in the workspace. Nothing outside the workspace changes.
Because the extension sets QUARTO_PYTHON, a project _environment file cannot override the selection. A wrong selection is corrected in the interpreter picker.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
Positron
Positron bundles the same Python extension and the same Quarto extension, so the steps are the same: open the folder, then run Python: Select Interpreter.
A workspace that already has an interpreter stored keeps it. python.defaultInterpreterPath in .vscode/settings.json applies only when no interpreter has been selected, so a stored choice is replaced through the picker. A change to that setting takes effect after Developer: Reload Window.
Positron opens a new terminal for each render, so the interpreter it passed to Quarto can be read there:
echo "QUARTO_PYTHON=[$QUARTO_PYTHON]"
An empty value means no interpreter is selected for the workspace.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
Other editors
An editor without Quarto integration, such as PhpStorm, leaves the choice to PATH. Activate the environment before starting the editor, or set QUARTO_PYTHON in its terminal or run configuration.
RStudio is in this group. It sets no QUARTO_PYTHON of its own, and Quarto does not read the Python preference that RStudio stores.

title: Python interpreters and editors
section: When no Python can host the kernel
text:
When no Python can host the kernel
juphyter install looks for an interpreter in this order: the one named by --python, then the one that owns the jupyter command on PATH, read from that script’s first line. When the interpreter it found has no ipykernel 7, it builds a virtual environment with JupyterLab instead of installing into the existing interpreter.
System and Homebrew Python builds are marked as externally managed, and pip install into them refuses. A virtual environment avoids that.

--create-venv PATH names where to build it.
Without --create-venv, the command asks before building one at ~/.venvs/juphyter, and builds it without asking when there is no terminal.
An environment that already exists at that path is reused, and its packages are installed again, so a second run finishes an interrupted one.
A directory that exists and holds something other than an environment is refused.
With --python, the command builds nothing. When the named interpreter has no ipykernel, it prints the pip install command for that interpreter and writes no kernel.
